The usual metrical pattern of the verb ἀΐω [I hear] in the tragedians is u u _, as at Pers. 633, Ag. 55, or _ u _ as at Suppl. 58 and Pers. 873 άϊον [I heard], which is the imperfect without augment. But in the choriambic verse Eum. 844 (repeated at 876) θυμὸν ἄϊε [hear my cry] has the measure of an amphibrach, as in Hesiod Op. 213 ὦ Πέρση, σὺ δ᾽ ἄϊε δίκης [O Perses, do you hear justice]. For thus, from Etym. M. p. 43, 5, the reading now found in the manuscripts, ἄκουε [listen], must be corrected. By the same interpolation in the manuscripts of Homer Od. 1, 352 ἀκουόντεσσι [to those listening] was introduced for ἀϊόντεσσι [to those hearing], which is to be restored from Plato's Republic p. 424b, where it is corrupted to ἀείδοντεσσι [to those singing], arising from the old spelling ἀειόντεσσι [to those hearing] (as in Hesychius ἀείοις: ἀκούοις [you might hear]): on which I have spoken in the Preface to the Oxford edition of Homer's Iliad, 1856, p. V.
And the highest one, hearing — the bird-voiced lament.
O Perses, do you hear justice
(with oblique cases αἰῶνος [of time], αἰῶνι [to time], αἰῶνα [time], except that once αἰώ [time] is used for αἰῶνα [time] at Ch. 350, about which more will be said below)
Thus Hermann probably corrected and supplemented what is read in M: Ζεὺς αἰῶνος κρέων ἀπαύστου [Zeus, ruler of unending time], the rest being omitted.

[But the reading at Pers. 1007, as the meter shows, is faulty: πεπλήγμεθ', οἷαι δι᾽ αἰῶνος τύχαι [we are struck, such fortunes through time], where a corrector in the margin of M wrote γρ. δαίμονος τύχαι [fortunes of a divinity], which could be διαίμονες τύχαι [divine fortunes], something like what is required by the meter.]

where αἰώ [time] for αἰῶνα [time] (as Ποσειδῶ [Poseidon] for Ποσειδῶνα [Poseidon] and other such forms are said) was restored by H. L. Ahrens. This form is noted in Bekk. Anecd. p. 363,17: αἰῶ τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ ἀποκοπὴν Αἰσχύλος [αἰώ for αἰῶνα by apocope in Aeschylus].
where τ' was added from Pearson's conjecture; O. Müller preferred αἰώ τε παρθένειον [and maiden time].
the fated lifetime was being fulfilled.
Zeus, ruler through unending time, appeared as the avenger of these things.
we are struck, such fortunes through time,
and he waits for a third lifetime.
the life of mortals is rich in flocks.
they considered maiden life as nothing,
and he passes through life unharmed.
for a woman deprives each man of life.
